original_question: If S^1(G) is a Segal algebra on a locally compact amenable group G, must S^1(G) be pseudo-amenable?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, the unnumbered open problem immediately after Theorem 4.3: "It is unknown whether or not S^1(G) is always pseudo-amenable when G is an amenable group." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right objects and the right implication direction: a Segal algebra S^1(G), a locally compact amenable group G, and the question whether amenability of G forces pseudo-amenability of S^1(G). That is exactly the unresolved issue isolated after Theorem 4.3, rather than the broader neighboring Question 12 about approximate amenability. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
missing_details: Make the quantifiers explicit: the paper is asking whether for every locally compact amenable group G and every Segal algebra S^1(G) on G, the algebra S^1(G) must be pseudo-amenable. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Specify the Banach-algebra setting: S^1(G) is a Segal algebra on G, i.e. a Segal subalgebra of L^1(G), considered with its usual convolution product. This is implicit in Section 4.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
Spell out the paper's definition of pseudo-amenable: by Definition 1.3, this means that S^1(G) has an approximate diagonal. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

State that no extra hypothesis such as SIN, abelian, compact, symmetric, or nontrivial/proper is part of the official pseudo-amenability question; the point is precisely whether the amenable SIN-group assumption in Theorem 4.3(3) can be dropped. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Include the nearby converse already known in the paper: Theorem 4.3(2) shows that if S^1(G) is pseudo-amenable, then G must be amenable, so the open issue is the converse direction. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Do not replace this with the broader adjacent Question 12, which asks whether every nontrivial Segal algebra is not approximately amenable; your draft is narrower and is about pseudo-amenability under amenability of G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

There are no hidden polynomial-style parameters here (field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers like 'for sufficiently large m'); the real hidden data are the Banach-algebra structure and the exact meaning of pseudo-amenable. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
refined_question: Let G be a locally compact amenable group, and let S^1(G) be a Segal algebra on G (equivalently, a Segal subalgebra of L^1(G) with the convolution product). Must S^1(G) be pseudo-amenable, in the sense of Definition 1.3, i.e. must it admit an approximate diagonal?
justification: The draft is already very close, but the nearest paper-faithful target is not a numbered question: it is the unnumbered sentence immediately following Theorem 4.3 in Section 4.1. The nearby context gives the exact scope. Theorem 4.3(2) supplies the necessary condition that pseudo-amenability of S^1(G) forces amenability of G, while Theorem 4.3(3) proves the converse only for amenable SIN-groups; the paper then states that it is unknown whether this converse holds for arbitrary amenable locally compact groups. Definition 1.3 supplies the exact meaning of pseudo-amenable used in the refined question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
